conventions.convention: Spacetime is a smooth Hausdorff second-countable boundaryless four-manifold with Lorentzian signature (-,+,+,+), a smooth time orientation, and an independent manifold orientation. Observers are future unit timelike vectors; congruences, charts, and tetrads are distinct objects.
Observer covectors are E_a=c F_ab n^b and B_a=−(★F)_ab n^b. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad adapted to n, F_0i=−E_i/c and F_ij=ε_ijk B_k, with ε_123=+1.
Use SI units, length coordinates with x⁰=ct, and j=cρn+J. The constants c and e have their exact SI defining values; μ₀ is experimentally determined, with no numerical value adopted; ε₀=(μ₀c²)⁻¹.
G_N>0 and Λ are primitive model parameters; κ_E=8πG_N/c⁴ has unit m/J. The independent optional normalization κ₀>0 has unit Wb and implies no charge quantization.
The curved Maxwell adoption is dF=0 and ∇_a F^{ab}=−μ₀j^b for smooth F and j on an open domain. It excludes singular sources, material excitation laws, and any assumption of a global potential.

The flat compatibility calculation uses nonempty open I and Ω, jointly C¹ fields and continuous sources. Its conclusions concern the Maxwell subsystem and force/power component dictionary; they assert neither a coupled Einstein solution nor empirical validity.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the selected model's smooth oriented time-oriented Lorentzian geometry, primitive electromagnetic two-form and current, observer-derived electric and magnetic covectors, SI constants and component units, gravitational parameters, and independent optional circle normalization.
For a smooth real electromagnetic two-form F and smooth four-current j on an open subset of the stated oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, adopt dF=0 and ∇^g_a F^{ab}=−μ₀j^b.

Under its stated flat inertial domain, regularity, SI, and component conventions, TM1 and TM2 hold if and only if the four displayed SI vacuum Maxwell equations hold. For f^ν=F^{νλ}j_λ, f⁰=(J·E)/c and fⁱ=ρE_i+(J×B)_i. This checks the Maxwell subsystem and local force dictionary, not the coupled Einstein equation.

published_dependencies.used_for: Lorentzian geometry, observer and frame definitions, local adapted tetrads, connection formula, curvature conventions, and length-coordinate units.

The oriented Lorentzian Hodge definition, ★²=−id on two-forms, basis signs, and exterior-derivative component formula. Source comparison also used [Tong §3.1.3](https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/gr/grhtml/S3.html).
Rest-covector positivity and the exact observer-field reconstruction and component dictionary.
Inherited SI constants, units, and measured μ₀ status; independently compared with [BIPM §2.3.1](https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/41483022/SI-Brochure-9.pdf).
Adopted flat spacetime interpretation, inertial descriptions, and shared clock/light conversion constant, without deriving Maxwell dynamics.
Published SI (-+++) tensor signs, raised components, observer dictionary, and current contraction conventions.
The four pointwise SI Maxwell equations at jointly C¹ field and continuous-source regularity; its weak branch is not invoked.
Proper orthochronous affine changes of inertial description and their adopted physical scope.
The inherited flat tensor/vector Maxwell equivalence and matching sourced-equation sign; it is formulation context for the curved adoption.
Continuous volume-source fields and the adopted four-current identification j=(cρ,J).
Coordinate partial derivatives used in the flat component calculation.
Spatial divergence and curl formulas and their C¹ requirements.
The right-handed spatial cross-product signs in the force-density contraction.
Adopted continuum force density ρE+J×B and power density J·E, conditional on an applicable explicitly stated matter model.

seams_checked.note: The inspected coupling and matter-model clauses preserve the supplier's geometry, SI units, κ_E and κ₀ distinction, and Maxwell source sign. They add separate gravitational, matter, or action assumptions; the supplier does not claim to establish those additions.

The topology definition preserves smooth real F, potential units, and the independent optional κ₀ normalization. The potentials theorem explicitly uses only the homogeneous Maxwell clause dF=0 and retains the exclusions of singular-domain sources, quantum charge quantization, and coupled Einstein-solution claims.
